summary: The root وَدْقٌ (wdq) refers to rain, which can be either gentle or violent. Some sources specifically define it as violent rain.
lane: وَدْقٌ ذ Rain, (S, K, TA,) whether violent or gentle: (TA:) or violent rain. (MF in art. قهب .)

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

headwords.def: وَدْقٌ Rain, (S, K, TA,) whether violent or gentle: (TA:) or violent rain. (MF in art. قهب .)
مُتَوَدِّقٌ : occurring in the TA, art. قهب ; from الوَدْقُ , meaning Violent rain. (MF.)

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
